title: Epochal Token Bridge & Attribution Orchestrator for Console Analytics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The console analytics stack currently has a split between the streaming metering pipeline (subsecond Kafka-based ingestion) and the month/epochal billing snapshot generator. This causes late-arrival credits, double-counting edge cases for multi-model route-splits, and opaque corrections during invoice generation. Goal: build an orchestrator (Epochal Token Bridge) that reliably maps streaming token events to durable, epochal billing atoms while preserving idempotency, provenance, and deterministic tie-breaks for overlapping attributions.

Scope:
- Ingest canonical streaming token events (token_claim, kv_cache_hit, prefix_reuse) from the existing event bus.
- Normalize events into a compact epochal shard format designed for downstream billing rollups: fields include tenant_id, session_id, epoch_window_id, route_tags, model_variant, token_count, token_type, compute_estimate_usd, event_fingerprint, and ingestion_watermark.
- Implement a deterministic fencing strategy (token_sequence_id + tenant_shard) to avoid duplicate attribution across retries and multi-path routing.
- Provide a migration path so the current snapshot generator can consume bridged atoms with backwards compatibility (translator layer).
- Surface per-epoch QA metrics and invariant checks to the console: balance checks, negative-credit detection, sudden-latency spikes, and coverage delta compared to the streaming ledger.

Architecture overview:
1) Sidecar coalescer: lightweight process colocated with ingestion tier consumes Kafka topic, performs prefix/KV caching lookups and emits a normalized record to a durable S3 staging bucket in compact Parquet/ORC shards partitioned by epoch_window_id and tenant_region.
2) Orchestrator controller: periodically schedules epochal compaction jobs that join staging shards with the session index, apply deterministic fencing, and write canonical epoch atoms to the billing write model (BigQuery/ClickHouse depending on tenant).
3) Translator layer: a small queryable service that exposes both the new epochal atom view and a legacy-compatible view for older billing jobs, including on-the-fly attribution heuristics for model_variant fallbacks.
4) Checkpoint manager: coordinated watermarks with zookeeper/raft-based lease to ensure exactly-once semantics for compaction windows and safe retries.

Invariant checks and metrics:
- Token conservation: total tokens in epochal atoms should be within 0.1% of streaming ledger for steady-state tenants (alert if >0.5%).
- Credit monotonicity: tenant credits must not decrease unexpectedly after compaction; any negative corrections require manual review workflow.
- Late arrival rate: fraction of tokens assigned to previous epoch windows. Aim for <0.3% after migration.

Data Q/A and rollout strategy:
- Phase 0 (shadow run): run sidecar coalescer to write staging shards; do not feed epochal atoms into billing. Run translator to compare outputs with legacy snapshot generator and compute diffs.
- Phase 1 (read-only canary): feed epochal atoms to a read-only billing validation cluster; compute reconciliation reports nightly and run automated invariants.
- Phase 2 (partial write): enable epochal atoms for a small set of tenants (<= 5% of revenue) with dual-write enabled and monitor reconciliation dashboards.
- Phase 3 (full cutover): migrate all tenants and deprecate legacy path after 4 weeks of stable metrics.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for deterministic fencing logic and watermark boundary conditions.
- Integration tests with a synthetic event generator that simulates out-of-order and duplicated messages.
- End-to-end shadow-run reports stored under Google Drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/Console/ENG-473210/shadow-reports.zip

Operational notes and rollback:
- Fast rollback plan: switch orchestrator lease to a "pause" state that stops compaction and reverts billing read models to legacy snapshot view. Post-rollback action: run a targeted compensation job to reconcile any partial writes.
- Alerts: high-severity pager if token conservation delta exceeds threshold or if compactor fails three consecutive epochs.

Deliverables:
- Sidecar coalescer service (Go) + schema migration for epoch atom.
- Orchestrator controller + translator service.
- Migration runbook, QA dashboards, and post-cutover audit report.

implementation_notes: Fencing approach: use 128-bit event_fingerprint (sha256 truncated) plus monotonic token_sequence_id anchored to tenant_shard. Avoid cross-tenant coordination; all conflict resolution must be local to tenant shard. Compactor will prefer higher compute_estimate_usd when tie-breaking model variant overlaps (product decision approved).
